strings.history.title: How the parties changed
strings.history.intro: Read it like a version-control history: each colored line is a party, with the newest events at the top. Lines join when parties merge or run together, and branch off when they split. Click a party to highlight its line and open its details.
strings.method.title: How to read this
strings.method.1: Each topic runs from 0 (the left label) to 10 (the right label). The ends describe the issue, not "left-wing" or "right-wing."
strings.method.2: Placements are editorial summaries of the cited reporting (party explainers, interviews, votes and statements). They are not scores the parties supplied themselves.
strings.method.3: When a party gave no clear position, or the reporting conflicts, it appears under "No clear position" instead of being guessed onto the line.
strings.method.4: Choose several elections to see them together: every marker carries its election year, and each election’s lists are separate entries. The Party history tab shows how parties merged and split.
strings.method.5: Click any party to open its stance and sources. Please check the sources before you rely on a placement.
